prompt: Write part of a deposition transcript (about 400 words) of a plaintiff in a car accident lawsuit. The defense lawyer asks (lines start with 'Q:') and the plaintiff answers (lines start with 'A:'). Accident: rear-end collision in Katy, Texas. Injury: neck and back strain. Ask about the accident, treatment and daily life. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1239; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather not put my full name in a transcript, but I understand this is a synthetic test document, so I'll just answer the questions.

Q: Thank you. Can you describe what you were doing right before the collision?
A: I was driving home from work on a weekday afternoon. Traffic had slowed down on the main road near the shopping center in Katy, so I was stopped behind a line of cars at a light.

Q: Were you wearing your seatbelt?
A: Yes, I was.

Q: Describe the impact for me.
A: The vehicle behind me hit my rear bumper. It wasn't a huge crash in terms of how the cars looked afterward, but my head snapped back and then forward against the headrest. I felt a sharp pain across my neck almost right away.

Q: Did you get out of the vehicle at the scene?
A: I did, but I felt stiff and sore. My lower back started aching within an hour or so.

Q: Did you seek medical care that day?
A: I went to an urgent care clinic the same evening. They checked my range of motion, took some X-rays, and diagnosed a neck and back strain.

Q: What treatment have you received since then?
A: I've had physical therapy about three times a week. I also got a prescription for muscle relaxers and an anti-inflammatory, and I've been using heat packs at home.

Q: How has the injury affected your daily routine?
A: Mostly in small ways that add up. I used to go to the gym regularly, and I've had to stop lifting. Sitting at my desk for long stretches makes my back stiff, so I have to get up every half hour. Turning my head to check my blind spot when I drive is uncomfortable, and I've asked my partner to handle the grocery runs because carrying bags aggravates my lower back.

Q: Have you missed any work?
A: I missed a few days early on and then came back on a modified schedule. I'm now able to do my job, but I take more breaks than I used to.

Q: Before this collision, did you have any prior problems with your neck or back?
A: I had occasional tightness from long days at a computer, but nothing that required treatment or stopped me from doing things I wanted to do.

Q: Do you currently have any restrictions from your doctor?
A: Yes. I've been told to avoid heavy lifting and repetitive twisting until my physical therapist clears me.
